scope: Two new disposable PostgreSQL 16.13 databases and a synthetic, quiescent four-record core only. No Eva1, live Eva, Hindsight, provider, connector, user archive, user object, volume or secret was read or changed.

checks.name: source export to distinct fresh target restore
restore and object-boundary regression without external state

proven: A synthetic source installation with one tenant, installation, current identity pack, current policy pack, principal, evidence envelope, source event, fact assertion and current-fact pointer exported as a complete 39-record-set archive.
The normal archive publication path ran its standalone reader validation before publication.
A distinct fresh PostgreSQL database reached the current migration head and restored exactly the nine source records in one serializable transaction.

The synthetic memory fact was written through Eva's ordinary memory authority and read back after restore. All other canonical record sets were present and empty; no action, worker, connector, credential or encrypted object was imported.
not_proven: This is not a real user backup, a full nonempty 39-table workload, an encrypted-object migration or an off-host restore.
The historical terminal reader fixture remains deliberately rejected because its internal fixture IDs conflict; this proof neither changes nor relabels it.
The two disposable PostgreSQL containers and the temporary PyNaCl target were removed after the checks.
The known Alembic dependency-cycle warning remains a warning only; it did not fail either migration or restore check.
